title: Walks that fail in the full sweep
goal: The scripted walks are the app driving itself, and some of them no longer reach what they were written to check. Find out what each failing walk is looking for, then either fix the app if the walk is right or update the walk if the app moved on. This serves the focus because the sweep is the only thing that tells a focus runner whether the change it just made broke anything: a sweep with failures nobody has named cannot say that, so every focus feature ships on a weaker claim than it should.

effects-open-into-view-walk and effects-room-for-the-one-you-opened-walk alternate pass/fail on the SAME build, and the cause is in the walks rather than in timing. Both press the Border twist TWICE in a row (steps 8 and 10 of effects-room-for-the-one-you-opened-walk), which returns the row to whatever state it started in, and the probe keeps that state between runs. So each run leaves the next one with the opposite answer. Reproduced on clean main, same build, three runs in a row: ok, failed, ok. Command: Scripts/playtest.sh Scripts/playtest/effects-room-for-the-one-you-opened-walk.json --no-build. Failure: 'step 32 (expect): the control called "Twist" in "Border" reads "Border, shut", not "Border, open"'. The fix these two want is a known starting state rather than another wait: neither walk declares what it needs in setup, and there is no forget word for which effect rows are open. Found while running the walks for a-shape-drawn-in-an-icon-frame-comes-in-at-a-wei; that task's change is not involved (it only moves stroke weights on icon frames, and these walks use no frames at all).

The arrow-parts one has a wider cause worth knowing: a scripted press does not reach a part's tick on ANY shape. Reproduced on a plain rectangle too, pressing Switch in Fill, and the app-side setOn closure never runs at all, which is why every other walk flips a part through an action (toggleFillSwitch) instead of pressing it.

Worth trying as ONE cause before diagnosing them one at a time: the 19 walks the last sweep named are mostly border-*, colour-* and copies-* walks, and a good number of those press a tick in Appearance or in the Effects list. If a scripted press cannot reach a SwiftUI tick at all (reproduced above on a plain rectangle, Switch in Fill, setOn never runs), that one fault would account for a whole block of them. The cheap check is to pick two from the list and see whether the step that fails is a press on a tick.
